title: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how closely it fits

sections.skill: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how closely it fits

questions.skill: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how closely it fits
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Draw a straight line that fits the data. Then write an equation of your line.
questions.prompt_markup: Draw a straight line that fits the data. Then write an equation of your line.
questions.correct_answer: The equation of the line drawn, about y = x + 0.5
questions.drawing_answer: A straight line close to the points, with about as many points above it as below it, for example through (0, 0.5) and (8, 8.5)
questions.grading_note: Slopes from about 0.8 to 1.2 and y-intercepts from about 0 to 1.5 are accepted when they match the line drawn.

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 10 and y from 0 to 10. x-axis label "x", y-axis label "y". Points: (1, 2), (2, 2), (3, 4), (4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 7), (7, 7), (8, 9).

questions.skill: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how closely it fits
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Draw a straight line that fits the data. Use your line to estimate y when x = 9.
questions.prompt_markup: Draw a straight line that fits the data. Use your line to estimate y when x = 9.
questions.correct_answer: About 1 to 2, read from the line drawn (y = -x + 10 gives 1)
questions.drawing_answer: A straight line close to the points, with about as many points above it as below it, for example through (0, 10) and (8, 2)
questions.grading_note: Accept an estimate that matches the student's own line.

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 10 and y from 0 to 10. x-axis label "x", y-axis label "y". Points: (1, 9), (2, 8), (3, 8), (4, 6), (5, 6), (6, 4), (7, 3), (8, 3).

questions.skill: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how closely it fits
questions.prompt: Two students drew lines for the same scatter plot. Line A has every point above it. Line B has about half the points above it and half below, all close to it. Which line fits better? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
Two students drew lines for the same scatter plot. Line A has every point above it. Line B has about half the points above it and half below, all close to it.
Which line fits better? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Line B, because the points are close to it and balanced on both sides.

questions.skill: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how closely it fits
questions.prompt: Why is the line on the scatter plot a poor fit?
questions.prompt_markup: Why is the line on the scatter plot a poor fit?

choices.text: It does not follow the upward trend of the points.
It passes through too many points.

questions.correct_answer: It does not follow the upward trend of the points.

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 10 and y from 0 to 10. x-axis label "x", y-axis label "y". Points: (1, 2), (2, 2), (3, 4), (4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 7), (7, 7), (8, 9). Straight line through (0, 4) and (10, 4).

questions.skill: Informally fit a straight line to a scatter plot and judge how closely it fits
questions.prompt: A line that fits a scatter plot well must pass through every point.
questions.prompt_markup: A line that fits a scatter plot well must pass through every point.
questions.grading_note: A good line is close to the points; it may pass through none of them.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Fit a least-squares line with technology and compare candidate lines
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Use a calculator or spreadsheet to find the least-squares line for the data (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 6), (4, 8), (5, 10), (6, 11). Round the slope and the y-intercept to the nearest tenth.
questions.prompt_markup: Use a calculator or spreadsheet to find the least-squares line for the data (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 6), (4, 8), (5, 10), (6, 11). Round the slope and the y-intercept to the nearest tenth.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Fit a least-squares line with technology and compare candidate lines
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Two lines are proposed for the data (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 6), (4, 8): y = 2x + 1 and y = 1.6x + 1.5. Find the sum of the squared residuals for each line. Which line fits better?
questions.prompt_markup:
Two lines are proposed for the data (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 6), (4, 8): y = 2x + 1 and y = 1.6x + 1.5.

questions.grading_note: Both sums and the conclusion are required.
